If He protects it from him, it is His Sanctuary and His House; and if He leaves it to him, by Allah, we have no way to defend it.”

He made food for them, and they made an alliance in Dhu al-Qaʿda, a sacred month. They bound themselves and promised by Allah to be one hand with the wronged against the wrongdoer until his right was returned to him, as long as the sea wets a tuft of wool and as long as Thabir and Hiraʾ stand in their places, and to help one another in their living. Quraysh called that alliance Hilf al-Fudul, and said: “These people have taken on something of great merit.” Then they walked to al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, took the man from Zubayd’s goods from him, and gave them back to him.
parts: Al-Zubayr {ˈibn} {ˈabdul muttˈɑlib} stood up about it and said: “This cannot be left.” So {hˈɑːʃim}, Zuhra and Taym {ˈibn} Murra gathered in the house of Abdullah {ˈibn} Judan. He made food for them, and they made an alliance in Dhu al-Qada, a sacred month. They bound themselves and promised by {allˈɑːh} to be one hand with the wronged against the wrongdoer until his right was returned to him, as long as the sea wets a tuft of wool and as long as Thabir and Hira stand in their places, and to help one another in their living. {kuɹˈaɪʃ} called that alliance Hilf al-Fudul, and said: “These people have taken on something of great merit.” Then they walked to al-As {ˈibn} Wail, took the man from Zubayd’s goods from him, and gave them back to him.

text: [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:] “I witnessed, in the house of ʿAbdullah ibn Judʿan, an alliance which, if I were called to it in Islam, I would answer. They allied to return what is owed to its rightful people, and that no wrongdoer would overpower someone wronged.”
parts: [The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, said:] “I witnessed, in the house of Abdullah {ˈibn} Judan, an alliance which, if I were called to it in Islam, I would answer. They allied to return what is owed to its rightful people, and that no wrongdoer would overpower someone wronged.”

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Khadija bint Khuwaylid was a merchant woman of standing and wealth. She would hire men to trade with her money for a share of the profit. When she heard about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, about the truthfulness of his speech, the greatness of his trustworthiness and the nobility of his character, she sent for him and offered him to go out to al-Sham trading with her money, and she would give him more than she gave the other traders, with a young man of hers called Maysara. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted it from her and went out with her goods, and her young man Maysara went with him, until he reached al-Sham.
parts: {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: {xadˈiːdʒa} bint Khuwaylid was a merchant woman of standing and wealth. She would hire men to trade with her money for a share of the profit. When she heard about the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, about the truthfulness of his speech, the greatness of his trustworthiness and the nobility of his character, she sent for him and offered him to go out to al-Sham trading with her money, and she would give him more than she gave the other traders, with a young man of hers called Maysara. The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, accepted it from her and went out with her goods, and her young man Maysara went with him, until he reached al-Sham.

text: When he came back to Makkah to Khadija with her goods, she sold what he had brought, and it came to double, or nearly.
parts: When he came back to {mˈakka} to {xadˈiːdʒa} with her goods, she sold what he had brought, and it came to double, or nearly.

text: “Son of my uncle, I wish to marry you because of our kinship, your standing among your people, your trustworthiness, your good character and the truthfulness of your speech.”
parts: “Son of my uncle, I wish to marry you because of our kinship, your standing among your people, your trustworthiness, your good character and the truthfulness of your speech.”

text: Ibn Hisham said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was twenty-five years old when he married Khadija. More than one of the people of knowledge told me so, among them Abu ʿAmr al-Madani.
parts: {ˈibn} Hisham said: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, was twenty-five years old when he married {xadˈiːdʒa}. More than one of the people of knowledge told me so, among them Abu Amr al-Madani.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: al-Fijar was twenty years after the Elephant. The building of the Kaʿbah was fifteen years after al-Fijar, and his being sent as a prophet was five years after its building.
parts: {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: al-Fijar was twenty years after the Elephant. The building of the Kabah was fifteen years after al-Fijar, and his being sent as a prophet was five years after its building.

text: When the Kaʿbah was built, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to carry stones.
parts: When the Kabah was built, the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, went to carry stones.

text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was thirty-five years old, Quraysh gathered to build the Kaʿbah. They had been wanting to do it, to give it a roof, but they were afraid to take it down. It was only loose stones laid without mortar, a little higher than a man, and they wanted to raise it and roof it.
parts: When the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, was thirty-five years old, {kuɹˈaɪʃ} gathered to build the Kabah. They had been wanting to do it, to give it a roof, but they were afraid to take it down. It was only loose stones laid without mortar, a little higher than a man, and they wanted to raise it and roof it.

text: The sea had thrown up a ship at Jeddah, belonging to a merchant of the Romans, and it was broken up. They took its timber and made it ready for the roof.
parts: The sea had thrown up a ship at Jeddah, belonging to a merchant of the Romans, and it was broken up. They took its timber and made it ready for the roof.

text: There was in Makkah a Coptic man who was a carpenter, and he got ready for them some of what was needed.
parts: There was in {mˈakka} a Coptic man who was a carpenter, and he got ready for them some of what was needed.

text: He said: “People of Quraysh, put nothing of your earnings into its building except what is good and lawful.”
parts: He said: “People of {kuɹˈaɪʃ}, put nothing of your earnings into its building except what is good and lawful.”

text: Then Quraysh divided the Kaʿbah between them. The side of the door was for Banu ʿAbd Manaf and Zuhra. Between the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner was for Banu Makhzum and the clans of Quraysh who joined them. The back of the Kaʿbah was for Banu Jumah and Sahm. The side of al-Hijr was for Banu ʿAbd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, Banu Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza and Banu ʿAdi ibn Kaʿb: that is al-Hatim.
parts: Then {kuɹˈaɪʃ} divided the Kabah between them. The side of the door was for Banu Abd Manaf and Zuhra. Between the Black Corner and the Yemeni Corner was for Banu Makhzum and the clans of {kuɹˈaɪʃ} who joined them. The back of the Kabah was for Banu Jumah and Sahm. The side of al-Hijr was for Banu Abd al-Dar {ˈibn} Qusayy, Banu Asad {ˈibn} Abd al-Uzza and Banu Adi {ˈibn} Kab: that is al-Hatim.

text: Then the people were afraid to take it down, and held back from it. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: “I will begin taking it down for you.” He took the pickaxe and stood on it, saying: “O Allah, no harm is meant. O Allah, we want nothing but good.” Then he took down part of it, at the two corners. The people waited that night and said: “We will see. If something happens to him, we will not take any of it down, and we will put it back as it was. If nothing happens to him, then Allah is pleased with what we have done in taking it down.” In the morning al-Walid went back to his work, and took it down, and the people took it down with him, until they reached the foundation, the foundation of Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Then the clans of Quraysh gathered stones to build it, each clan gathering on its own. Then they built it until the building reached the place of the Corner [the Black Stone], and they quarrelled over it: every clan wanted to raise it to its place, and not the others.

Then they built it until the building reached the place of the Corner [the Black Stone], and they quarrelled over it: every clan wanted to raise it to its place, and not the others.

text: Quraysh stayed like that for four or five nights. Then they gathered in the Mosque, consulted one another and agreed to be fair.
parts: {kuɹˈaɪʃ} stayed like that for four or five nights. Then they gathered in the Mosque, consulted one another and agreed to be fair.

text: Some of the narrators claim that Abu Umayya ibn al-Mughira ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzum, who was then the oldest man in all of Quraysh, said: “People of Quraysh, let the first person who comes in through the gate of this Mosque judge between you in what you disagree about.” And they did so.
parts: Some of the narrators claim that Abu Umayya {ˈibn} al-Mughira {ˈibn} Abdullah {ˈibn} Amr {ˈibn} Makhzum, who was then the oldest man in all of {kuɹˈaɪʃ}, said: “People of {kuɹˈaɪʃ}, let the first person who comes in through the gate of this Mosque judge between you in what you disagree about.” And they did so.

text: The first one to come in was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they saw him, they said: “This is al-Amin, the trustworthy one. We are content. This is Muhammad.” When he reached them and they told him about it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Bring me a cloth.” It was brought, and he took the Corner [the Black Stone] and placed it in it with his own hand. Then he said: “Let each clan take hold of a side of the cloth, then lift it all together.” They did so, until when they had brought it to its place, he set it there with his own hand ﷺ. Then the building went on over it. Quraysh used to call the Messenger of Allah ﷺ al-Amin.

text: … and the first thing of the Mighty Qurʾan to be sent down to him. That was when he ﷺ was forty years old.
parts: … and the first thing of the Mighty {kʊɹˈɑːn} to be sent down to him. That was when he , peace be upon him, was forty years old.

text: Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib that he was forty-three years old at that time.
parts: {ˈibn} Jarir reported from {ˈibn} Abbas and Said {ˈibn} al-Musayyib that he was forty-three years old at that time.

text: [Hiraʾ] is a mountain in upper Makkah, three miles from it, on the left of whoever goes to Mina. It has a peak that leans over, facing the Kaʿbah, and the cave is in that bend.
parts: [Hira] is a mountain in upper {mˈakka}, three miles from it, on the left of whoever goes to Mina. It has a peak that leans over, facing the Kabah, and the cave is in that bend.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stay at Hiraʾ for one month every year, in devotion. That was something Quraysh held dear in the time before Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would stay that month every year, feeding the poor who came to him. When he had finished his month, the first thing he did when he left, before going into his house, was go to the Kaʿbah and go round it seven times, or as many as Allah willed. Then he would go back to his house.

text: [ʿAʾisha said:] The first of the revelation that came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was true dreams in his sleep. He did not see a dream but it came true like the breaking of dawn.
parts: [Aisha said:] The first of the revelation that came to the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, was true dreams in his sleep. He did not see a dream but it came true like the breaking of dawn.

text: Then being alone was made dear to him. He would go alone to the cave of Hiraʾ and worship there for a number of nights, before going back to his family, and he would take provisions for that. Then he would go back to Khadija and take provisions for the same again, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hiraʾ.
parts: Then being alone was made dear to him. He would go alone to the cave of Hira and worship there for a number of nights, before going back to his family, and he would take provisions for that. Then he would go back to {xadˈiːdʒa} and take provisions for the same again, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira.

text: The angel came to him and said: “Read.” He said: “I am not one who reads.” He said: “Then he took hold of me and pressed me until I was exhausted, then let me go and said: ‘Read.’ I said: ‘I am not one who reads.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a second time until I was exhausted, then let me go and said: ‘Read.’ I said: ‘I am not one who reads.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a third time until I was exhausted. Then he let me go and said:”

Then he let me go and said:”

text: The correct view is that his words “I am not one who reads” are a denial: that is, “I am not someone who knows how to read.”
parts: The correct view is that his words “I am not one who reads” are a denial: that is, “I am not someone who knows how to read.”

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back with them, his heart trembling, and went in to Khadija bint Khuwaylid. He said: “Cover me, cover me.” They covered him until the fear left him. He told Khadija what had happened and said to her: “I feared for myself.”
parts: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, went back with them, his heart trembling, and went in to {xadˈiːdʒa} bint Khuwaylid. He said: “Cover me, cover me.” They covered him until the fear left him. He told {xadˈiːdʒa} what had happened and said to her: “I feared for myself.”

text: Khadija said: “No, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep the ties of kinship, you honour the guest, you carry the burden of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, and you help in the hardships that come by right.”
parts: {xadˈiːdʒa} said: “No, by {allˈɑːh}, {allˈɑːh} will never disgrace you. You keep the ties of kinship, you honour the guest, you carry the burden of the weak, you give to those who have nothing, and you help in the hardships that come by right.”

text: Then Khadija took him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, Khadija’s cousin. He had become a Christian in the time before Islam. He used to write in Hebrew, and wrote from the Injil in Hebrew as much as Allah willed. He was a very old man who had become blind. Khadija said to him: “Cousin, listen to your nephew.” Waraqa said: “Nephew, what do you see?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told him what he had seen. Waraqa said: “This is the Namus who came down to Musa. I wish I were young now. I wish I could be alive when your people drive you out.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Will they drive me out?” He said: “Yes. No man has ever brought what you have brought without being treated as an enemy. If I live to see your day, I will support you with all my strength.”

text: Then before long Waraqa died, and the revelation paused for a while.

text: [He ﷺ said:] “While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hiraʾ, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was afraid of him. I went back and said: ‘Cover me, cover me.’ Then Allah sent down:”

I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was afraid of him. I went back and said: ‘Cover me, cover me.’ Then {allˈɑːh} sent down:”

text: So said ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir and more than one of the scholars: that revelation came to him on a Monday. There is no disagreement among them about this.

text: Then it was said: that was in the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal.
parts: Then it was said: that was in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.

text: The well-known view is that he was sent as a prophet in the month of Ramadan, as ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others stated.

text: Al-Waqidi narrated with his chain from Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir: the revelation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began on a Monday, the seventeenth night of Ramadan. And it was said: on the twenty-fourth of it.
parts: Al-Waqidi narrated with his chain from Abu Jafar al-Baqir: the revelation to the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, began on a Monday, the seventeenth night of {ɹamadˈɑːn}. And it was said: on the twenty-fourth of it.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to speak of all that Allah had blessed him and His servants with, of prophethood, in secret, to those of his family he trusted.
parts: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, began to speak of all that {allˈɑːh} had blessed him and His servants with, of prophethood, in secret, to those of his family he trusted.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Khadija was the first to believe in Allah and His Messenger, and to accept as true what he brought.

text: Then ʿAli ibn Abi Talib came a day after that, while the two of them were praying. ʿAli said: “Muhammad, what is this?” He said: “The religion of Allah, which He chose for Himself and sent His messengers with. I call you to Allah alone, who has no partner, and to His worship, and to reject al-Lat and al-ʿUzza.” ʿAli said: “This is something I have never heard of before today. I will not decide anything until I have spoken to Abu Talib.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not want his secret spread before his call was made public, so he said: “ʿAli, if you do not accept Islam, then keep it to yourself.” ʿAli stayed that night, and then Allah put Islam into ʿAli’s heart. In the morning he came early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “What did you offer me, Muhammad?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “That you bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, who has no partner, reject al-Lat and al-ʿUzza, and free yourself of false gods.” ʿAli did so, and accepted Islam.

text: Ibn Haritha, meaning Zayd, accepted Islam too. The two of them stayed like that for nearly a month, with ʿAli coming and going to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

text: [ʿAfif said:] I was a merchant, and I came to Mina in the days of the Hajj. Al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib was a merchant too, and I went to him to buy and sell. While we were with him, a man came out of a tent and stood praying facing the Kaʿbah. Then a woman came out and stood praying with him, and a boy came out and stood praying with him. I said: “ʿAbbas, what is this religion? We do not know what it is.” He said: “This is Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah. He says that Allah has sent him with it, and that the treasures of Kisra and Qaysar will be opened to him. This is his wife Khadija bint Khuwaylid, who believes in him, and this boy is his cousin ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who believes in him.” ʿAfif said: “If only I had believed that day, so that I could have been the second.”

text: The first to hurry to believe were: of the free men, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq; of the boys, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib; of the women, Khadija bint Khuwaylid, his wife, peace be upon him; and of the freed slaves, his freed slave Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi, may Allah be pleased with them all.
parts: The first to hurry to believe were: of the free men, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq; of the boys, Ali {ˈibn} Abi Talib; of the women, {xadˈiːdʒa} bint Khuwaylid, his wife, peace be upon him; and of the freed slaves, his freed slave Zayd {ˈibn} Haritha al-Kalbi, may {allˈɑːh} be pleased with them all.

text: Others said: the first of this Ummah to accept Islam was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

text: Al-Kalbi said: he [ʿAli] accepted Islam when he was nine years old.
parts: Al-Kalbi said: he [Ali] accepted Islam when he was nine years old.

text: The first of the free men to accept Islam was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and his Islam brought more benefit than that of those mentioned before, because he was a man of high standing, an honoured chief in Quraysh, a man of wealth, and one who called others to Islam. He was loved and brought people together, and spent his wealth in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

text: [Abu Bakr] was a merchant of good character and kindness. The men of his people would come to him and enjoy his company for more than one reason: his knowledge, his trade and his good company.
parts: [Abu Bakr] was a merchant of good character and kindness. The men of his people would come to him and enjoy his company for more than one reason: his knowledge, his trade and his good company.

text: He began to call to Islam those of his people he trusted, who came and sat with him. At his hands, as I have been told, these accepted Islam: al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam, ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, Talha ibn ʿUbaydullah, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, may Allah be pleased with them.
parts: He began to call to Islam those of his people he trusted, who came and sat with him. At his hands, as I have been told, these accepted Islam: al-Zubayr {ˈibn} al-Awwam, Uthman {ˈibn} Affan, Talha {ˈibn} Ubaydullah, Sad {ˈibn} Abi Waqqas and Abd al-Rahman {ˈibn} Awf, may {allˈɑːh} be pleased with them.

text: They went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with Abu Bakr. He offered them Islam, recited the Qurʾan to them and told them the truth of Islam, and they believed. These were the eight who came before [the people] to Islam. They believed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and believed in what came from Allah.
parts: They went to the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, with Abu Bakr. He offered them Islam, recited the {kʊɹˈɑːn} to them and told them the truth of Islam, and they believed. These were the eight who came before [the people] to Islam. They believed the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, and believed in what came from {allˈɑːh}.

text: Then people entered [Islam] in group after group, men and women, until the news of Islam spread in Makkah and people talked about it.
parts: Then people entered [Islam] in group after group, men and women, until the news of Islam spread in {mˈakka} and people talked about it.

text: When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, they would go out into the mountain passes and hide their prayer from their people.
parts: When the Companions of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, prayed, they would go out into the mountain passes and hide their prayer from their people.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Then, three years after he was sent, Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to proclaim openly what he had been commanded, and to be patient with the harm of the idol-worshippers.
parts: {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: Then, three years after he was sent, {allˈɑːh} commanded His Messenger , peace be upon him, to proclaim openly what he had been commanded, and to be patient with the harm of the idol-worshippers.

text: [Ibn ʿAbbas said:] When Allah sent down “And warn your nearest relatives” [al-Shuʿaraʾ 214], the Prophet ﷺ came to al-Safa, climbed it, and called out: “Ya sabahah!”, the call of alarm. The people gathered to him, some coming themselves and some sending someone. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib, Banu Fihr, Banu Kaʿb, if I told you that horsemen at the foot of this mountain wanted to attack you, would you believe me?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then I am a warner to you, before a severe punishment.”
parts: [{ˈibn} Abbas said:] When {allˈɑːh} sent down “And warn your nearest relatives” [al-Shuara 214], the Prophet , peace be upon him, came to al-Safa, climbed it, and called out: “Ya sabahah!”, the call of alarm. The people gathered to him, some coming themselves and some sending someone. The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, said: “Banu {ˈabdul muttˈɑlib}, Banu Fihr, Banu Kab, if I told you that horsemen at the foot of this mountain wanted to attack you, would you believe me?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then I am a warner to you, before a severe punishment.”

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Then they turned on those of his Companions who had accepted Islam and followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Every clan set upon the Muslims among them, imprisoning them and tormenting them with beatings, hunger and thirst, and with the burning ground of Makkah when the heat was fierce: those they could overpower, to turn them away from their religion. Some gave way because of the severity of what struck them, and some stood firm against them, and Allah protected them.
parts: {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: Then they turned on those of his Companions who had accepted Islam and followed the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,. Every clan set upon the Muslims among them, imprisoning them and tormenting them with beatings, hunger and thirst, and with the burning ground of {mˈakka} when the heat was fierce: those they could overpower, to turn them away from their religion. Some gave way because of the severity of what struck them, and some stood firm against them, and {allˈɑːh} protected them.

text: Bilal, [later] the freed slave of Abu Bakr, belonged to some of Banu Jumah, born a slave among them. He was Bilal ibn Rabah, and his mother’s name was Hamama. He was true in his Islam and pure of heart.
parts: {bilˈɑːl}, [later] the freed slave of Abu Bakr, belonged to some of Banu Jumah, born a slave among them. He was {bilˈɑːl} {ˈibn} Rabah, and his mother’s name was Hamama. He was true in his Islam and pure of heart.

text: [Ibn Masʿud] said: The first to show their Islam openly were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ʿAmmar, his mother Sumayya, Suhayb, Bilal and al-Miqdad. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah protected him through his uncle [Abu Talib], and Abu Bakr, Allah protected him through his people. As for the rest, the idol-worshippers seized them, put iron armour on them and left them in the scorching sun. Every one of them gave them what they wanted [with their tongues], except Bilal: his own self meant little to him for the sake of Allah, and he meant little to his people. They took him and handed him to the boys, who led him around the passes of Makkah while he said: “Ahad, Ahad”, One, One.
parts: [{ˈibn} Masud] said: The first to show their Islam openly were seven: the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, Abu Bakr, Ammar, his mother Sumayya, Suhayb, {bilˈɑːl} and al-Miqdad. The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, {allˈɑːh} protected him through his uncle [Abu Talib], and Abu Bakr, {allˈɑːh} protected him through his people. As for the rest, the idol-worshippers seized them, put iron armour on them and left them in the scorching sun. Every one of them gave them what they wanted [with their tongues], except {bilˈɑːl}: his own self meant little to him for the sake of {allˈɑːh}, and he meant little to his people. They took him and handed him to the boys, who led him around the passes of {mˈakka} while he said: “Ahad, Ahad”, One, One.

text: Waraqa ibn Nawfal used to pass by him while he was being tormented for it and was saying “Ahad, Ahad”, and Waraqa would say: “One, One, by Allah, Bilal.” Then he would turn to Umayya ibn Khalaf and those of Banu Jumah who did that to him and say: “I swear by Allah, if you kill him for this, I will make his grave a place of mercy.”
parts: Waraqa {ˈibn} Nawfal used to pass by him while he was being tormented for it and was saying “Ahad, Ahad”, and Waraqa would say: “One, One, by {allˈɑːh}, {bilˈɑːl}.” Then he would turn to Umayya {ˈibn} Khalaf and those of Banu Jumah who did that to him and say: “I swear by {allˈɑːh}, if you kill him for this, I will make his grave a place of mercy.”

text: I say: Some have found this difficult, because Waraqa died after the sending, during the pause in revelation, and people only accepted Islam after “O you wrapped up” was sent down. So how could Waraqa have passed by Bilal while he was tormented? This needs looking into.
parts: I say: Some have found this difficult, because Waraqa died after the sending, during the pause in revelation, and people only accepted Islam after “O you wrapped up” was sent down. So how could Waraqa have passed by {bilˈɑːl} while he was tormented? This needs looking into.

text: Then Ibn Ishaq mentions Abu Bakr passing by Bilal while he was being tormented. He bought him from Umayya in exchange for a slave of his, set him free, and released him from the torment.
parts: Then {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} mentions Abu Bakr passing by {bilˈɑːl} while he was being tormented. He bought him from Umayya in exchange for a slave of his, set him free, and released him from the torment.

text: And al-Nahdiyya and her daughter: he bought them from Banu ʿAbd al-Dar. Their mistress had sent them to grind flour for her, and he heard her say to them: “By Allah, I will never free you.” Abu Bakr said: “Release yourself from that oath, Umm so-and-so.” She said: “You release yourself! You have spoilt them, so free them yourself.” He said: “How much are they?” She said: “Such and such.” He said: “I have taken them, and they are free. Give her back her flour.” They said: “Shall we not finish grinding it first, Abu Bakr, and then give it back to her?” He said: “That too, if you wish.”
parts: And al-Nahdiyya and her daughter: he bought them from Banu Abd al-Dar. Their mistress had sent them to grind flour for her, and he heard her say to them: “By {allˈɑːh}, I will never free you.” Abu Bakr said: “Release yourself from that oath, Umm so-and-so.” She said: “You release yourself! You have spoilt them, so free them yourself.” He said: “How much are they?” She said: “Such and such.” He said: “I have taken them, and they are free. Give her back her flour.” They said: “Shall we not finish grinding it first, Abu Bakr, and then give it back to her?” He said: “That too, if you wish.”

text: Abu Quhafa said to his son Abu Bakr: “My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only, when you did what you did, you had freed strong men who would protect you and stand up for you.” Abu Bakr said: “Father, I only want what I want.”
parts: Abu Quhafa said to his son Abu Bakr: “My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only, when you did what you did, you had freed strong men who would protect you and stand up for you.” Abu Bakr said: “Father, I only want what I want.”

text: It is said that these verses were sent down about him and what his father said: [Surah al-Layl, verses 5 to 7].
parts: It is said that these verses were sent down about him and what his father said: [{sˈuːɹa} al-Layl, verses 5 to 7].

text: Banu Makhzum used to take ʿAmmar ibn Yasir out, with his father and his mother, who were a family of Islam, when the midday heat was fierce, and torment them on the burning ground of Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pass by them and say, as I have been told: “Patience, family of Yasir: your meeting place is Paradise.”
parts: Banu Makhzum used to take Ammar {ˈibn} Yasir out, with his father and his mother, who were a family of Islam, when the midday heat was fierce, and torment them on the burning ground of {mˈakka}. The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, would pass by them and say, as I have been told: “Patience, family of Yasir: your meeting place is Paradise.”

text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the trials that struck his Companions, while he himself was kept safe by his standing with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and by his uncle Abu Talib, and that he could not protect them from what they were suffering, he said to them: “What if you went out to the land of Abyssinia? There is a king there under whom no one is wronged, and it is a land of truthfulness, until Allah gives you a way out of what you are in.” So the Muslims among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the land of Abyssinia, fearing to be turned from their religion, and fleeing to Allah with their religion.
parts: When the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, saw the trials that struck his Companions, while he himself was kept safe by his standing with {allˈɑːh}, Mighty and Majestic, and by his uncle Abu Talib, and that he could not protect them from what they were suffering, he said to them: “What if you went out to the land of Abyssinia? There is a king there under whom no one is wronged, and it is a land of truthfulness, until {allˈɑːh} gives you a way out of what you are in.” So the Muslims among the Companions of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, went out to the land of Abyssinia, fearing to be turned from their religion, and fleeing to {allˈɑːh} with their religion.

text: It was the first emigration in Islam. The first of the Muslims to go out were ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan and his wife Ruqayya, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
parts: It was the first emigration in Islam. The first of the Muslims to go out were Uthman {ˈibn} Affan and his wife Ruqayya, the daughter of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,.

text: Al-Waqidi narrated that they set out for it in Rajab, in the fifth year after the sending, and that the first of them to emigrate were eleven men and four women. They reached the sea, some walking and some riding, and hired a ship to Abyssinia for half a dinar.
parts: Al-Waqidi narrated that they set out for it in Rajab, in the fifth year after the sending, and that the first of them to emigrate were eleven men and four women. They reached the sea, some walking and some riding, and hired a ship to Abyssinia for half a dinar.

text: Others said: rather, they were eighty-two men, besides their wives and children, and ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, about whom there is doubt. If he was among them, they were eighty-three men.
parts: Others said: rather, they were eighty-two men, besides their wives and children, and Ammar {ˈibn} Yasir, about whom there is doubt. If he was among them, they were eighty-three men.

text: [Umm Salama said:] So we went out to it in groups until we had all gathered there. We settled in the best of homes, next to the best of neighbours, safe in our religion, and we feared no wrong there.
parts: [Umm Salama said:] So we went out to it in groups until we had all gathered there. We settled in the best of homes, next to the best of neighbours, safe in our religion, and we feared no wrong there.

text: When Quraysh saw that we had found a home and safety, they were jealous of us. They agreed to send to the Negus about us, to have us driven out of his land and sent back to them. They sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Rabiʿa, and gathered gifts for him and for his generals, and did not leave out a single general without preparing a gift for him.
parts: When {kuɹˈaɪʃ} saw that we had found a home and safety, they were jealous of us. They agreed to send to the Negus about us, to have us driven out of his land and sent back to them. They sent Amr {ˈibn} al-As and Abdullah {ˈibn} Abi Rabia, and gathered gifts for him and for his generals, and did not leave out a single general without preparing a gift for him.

text: One of the gifts from Makkah he liked best was leather.
parts: One of the gifts from {mˈakka} he liked best was leather.

text: He became angry and said: “No, by the life of Allah! I will not hand them back until I have called them, spoken to them and seen what their matter is. They are people who sought refuge in my land and chose my protection over anyone else’s. If they are as these men say, I will hand them back. If they are otherwise, I will protect them and not come between them and their people, and I will not please these two.”
parts: He became angry and said: “No, by the life of {allˈɑːh}! I will not hand them back until I have called them, spoken to them and seen what their matter is. They are people who sought refuge in my land and chose my protection over anyone else’s. If they are as these men say, I will hand them back. If they are otherwise, I will protect them and not come between them and their people, and I will not please these two.”

text: The Negus said to him: “What is this religion you follow? You have left the religion of your people, and you have not entered Judaism or Christianity.” Jaʿfar said: “O King, we were a people of idol-worship. We worshipped idols, ate dead animals and treated our neighbours badly. We made lawful among ourselves what is sacred, shedding blood and more, holding nothing lawful or unlawful. Then Allah sent us a prophet from among ourselves, whose faithfulness, truthfulness and trustworthiness we knew. He called us to worship Allah alone, with no partner, to keep the ties of kinship, to protect our neighbours, and to pray and fast for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to worship none but Him.”
parts: The Negus said to him: “What is this religion you follow? You have left the religion of your people, and you have not entered Judaism or Christianity.” Jafar said: “O King, we were a people of idol-worship. We worshipped idols, ate dead animals and treated our neighbours badly. We made lawful among ourselves what is sacred, shedding blood and more, holding nothing lawful or unlawful. Then {allˈɑːh} sent us a prophet from among ourselves, whose faithfulness, truthfulness and trustworthiness we knew. He called us to worship {allˈɑːh} alone, with no partner, to keep the ties of kinship, to protect our neighbours, and to pray and fast for {allˈɑːh}, Mighty and Majestic, and to worship none but Him.”

text: In Ziyad’s version from Ibn Ishaq: “He called us to Allah, to declare Him One and worship Him, and to leave the stones and idols that we and our fathers worshipped besides Him. He commanded us to speak the truth, to fulfil trusts, to keep the ties of kinship, to be good neighbours, and to keep away from forbidden things and from bloodshed. He forbade us shameful deeds, false speech, eating the wealth of the orphan and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and commanded us prayer, zakat and fasting.”
parts: In Ziyad’s version from {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk}: “He called us to {allˈɑːh}, to declare Him One and worship Him, and to leave the stones and idols that we and our fathers worshipped besides Him. He commanded us to speak the truth, to fulfil trusts, to keep the ties of kinship, to be good neighbours, and to keep away from forbidden things and from bloodshed. He forbade us shameful deeds, false speech, eating the wealth of the orphan and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship {allˈɑːh} and associate nothing with Him, and commanded us prayer, zakat and fasting.”

text: “So we believed him, had faith in him and followed him in what he brought from Allah. We worshipped Allah alone with no partner and associated nothing with Him, held unlawful what was made unlawful for us and lawful what was made lawful for us. Then our people attacked us and tormented us, to turn us from our religion, to take us back from the worship of Allah to the worship of idols, and to make lawful again the bad things we used to make lawful. When they overpowered us, wronged us, made life narrow for us and came between us and our religion, we came out to your land. We chose you over everyone else, wished for your protection, and hoped we would not be wronged with you, O King.”
parts: “So we believed him, had faith in him and followed him in what he brought from {allˈɑːh}. We worshipped {allˈɑːh} alone with no partner and associated nothing with Him, held unlawful what was made unlawful for us and lawful what was made lawful for us. Then our people attacked us and tormented us, to turn us from our religion, to take us back from the worship of {allˈɑːh} to the worship of idols, and to make lawful again the bad things we used to make lawful. When they overpowered us, wronged us, made life narrow for us and came between us and our religion, we came out to your land. We chose you over everyone else, wished for your protection, and hoped we would not be wronged with you, O King.”

text: He said: “Come, recite to me some of what he brought.” So he recited to him the beginning of Kaf Ha Ya ʿAyn Sad [Surah Maryam]. By Allah, the Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their scrolls were wet [when they heard what he recited to them]. Then he said [to them]: “This speech comes from the same lamp-niche that Musa brought. Go, rightly guided. No, by Allah, I will not hand them over to you, and I will not please you.”
parts: He said: “Come, recite to me some of what he brought.” So he recited to him the beginning of Kaf Ha Ya Ayn Sad [{sˈuːɹa} {mˈaɹjam}]. By {allˈɑːh}, the Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their scrolls were wet [when they heard what he recited to them]. Then he said [to them]: “This speech comes from the same lamp-niche that {mˈuːsa} brought. Go, rightly guided. No, by {allˈɑːh}, I will not hand them over to you, and I will not please you.”

text: Jaʿfar said to him: “We say: he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, His spirit and His word, which He cast into Maryam, the virgin, devoted to Allah.” The Negus lowered his hand to the ground and took a little stick between his fingers, and said: “ʿIsa ibn Maryam is not more than what you have said by the length of this little stick.”
parts: Jafar said to him: “We say: he is the servant of {allˈɑːh} and His messenger, His spirit and His word, which He cast into {mˈaɹjam}, the virgin, devoted to {allˈɑːh}.” The Negus lowered his hand to the ground and took a little stick between his fingers, and said: “Isa {ˈibn} {mˈaɹjam} is not more than what you have said by the length of this little stick.”

text: “Go: you are suyum in the land”, that is, safe in the land. “Whoever insults you will pay a fine. Whoever insults you will pay a fine. Whoever insults you will pay a fine”, three times. “I would not want a dabr, and to have hurt one man of you.”
parts: “Go: you are suyum in the land”, that is, safe in the land. “Whoever insults you will pay a fine. Whoever insults you will pay a fine. Whoever insults you will pay a fine”, three times. “I would not want a dabr, and to have hurt one man of you.”

text: When Abu Talib saw what the people were doing, he gathered Banu ʿAbd al-Muttalib and told them to bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into their valley and protect him from those who wanted to kill him. The Muslims and the non-Muslims among them agreed on this: some did it out of family loyalty, and some out of faith and certainty.
parts: When Abu Talib saw what the people were doing, he gathered Banu {ˈabdul muttˈɑlib} and told them to bring the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, into their valley and protect him from those who wanted to kill him. The Muslims and the non-Muslims among them agreed on this: some did it out of family loyalty, and some out of faith and certainty.

text: The idol-worshippers of Quraysh met and agreed not to sit with them, not to trade with them and not to enter their houses, until they handed over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to be killed. In their plotting they wrote a document of pledges and promises never to accept peace from Banu Hashim and never to show them pity until they handed him over.
parts: The idol-worshippers of {kuɹˈaɪʃ} met and agreed not to sit with them, not to trade with them and not to enter their houses, until they handed over the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, to be killed. In their plotting they wrote a document of pledges and promises never to accept peace from Banu {hˈɑːʃim} and never to show them pity until they handed him over.

text: Banu Hashim stayed in their valley for three years, and the hardship and strain on them grew severe. Quraysh cut them off from the markets: of the food that came to Makkah and the goods for sale, they let none reach them, but hurried to it first and bought it.
parts: Banu {hˈɑːʃim} stayed in their valley for three years, and the hardship and strain on them grew severe. {kuɹˈaɪʃ} cut them off from the markets: of the food that came to {mˈakka} and the goods for sale, they let none reach them, but hurried to it first and bought it.

text: When people went to bed, Abu Talib would tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to lie down on his own bed, so that anyone who meant to harm him by a plot or a sudden attack would see it. Then, when people were asleep, he would tell one of his sons, his brothers or his cousins to lie down on the bed of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to go to one of their beds and sleep there.
parts: When people went to bed, Abu Talib would tell the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, to lie down on his own bed, so that anyone who meant to harm him by a plot or a sudden attack would see it. Then, when people were asleep, he would tell one of his sons, his brothers or his cousins to lie down on the bed of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, and tell the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, to go to one of their beds and sleep there.

text: At the end of three years, men of Banu ʿAbd Manaf, of Qusayy, and others of Quraysh whose mothers were from Banu Hashim, began to blame one another. They saw that they had cut the ties of kinship and made light of what was right. That same night they agreed to break the treacherous pact they had made, and to free themselves of it.
parts: At the end of three years, men of Banu Abd Manaf, of Qusayy, and others of {kuɹˈaɪʃ} whose mothers were from Banu {hˈɑːʃim}, began to blame one another. They saw that they had cut the ties of kinship and made light of what was right. That same night they agreed to break the treacherous pact they had made, and to free themselves of it.

text: And Allah sent the termite against their document, and it ate away every pledge and promise in it.
parts: And {allˈɑːh} sent the termite against their document, and it ate away every pledge and promise in it.

text: It is said that it was hung up in the roof of the House. It left no name of Allah in it without eating it away, and what remained in it was idol-worship, wrongdoing and the cutting of kinship.
parts: It is said that it was hung up in the roof of the House. It left no name of {allˈɑːh} in it without eating it away, and what remained in it was idol-worship, wrongdoing and the cutting of kinship.

text: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Khadija and Abu Talib died in the same year.
parts: {muhˈammad} {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: {xadˈiːdʒa} and Abu Talib died in the same year.

text: Al-Bayhaqi said: It has reached me that Khadija died three days after Abu Talib.
parts: Al-Bayhaqi said: It has reached me that {xadˈiːdʒa} died three days after Abu Talib.

text: Al-Waqidi claimed that Khadija and Abu Talib died three years before the Hijrah, in the year they came out of the valley, and that Khadija died thirty-five nights before Abu Talib.
parts: Al-Waqidi claimed that {xadˈiːdʒa} and Abu Talib died three years before the Hijrah, in the year they came out of the valley, and that {xadˈiːdʒa} died thirty-five nights before Abu Talib.

text: [He ﷺ said:] “Quraysh did nothing to me that I disliked until Abu Talib died.”
parts: [He , peace be upon him, said:] “{kuɹˈaɪʃ} did nothing to me that I disliked until Abu Talib died.”

text: When Abu Talib died, Quraysh did harm to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they had never done in his uncle Abu Talib’s lifetime. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to al-Taʾif, seeking help and protection from Thaqif against his people, and hoping they would accept from him what he brought them from Allah, Most High. He went out to them alone.
parts: When Abu Talib died, {kuɹˈaɪʃ} did harm to the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, that they had never done in his uncle Abu Talib’s lifetime. So the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, went out to al-Taif, seeking help and protection from {θakˈiːf} against his people, and hoping they would accept from him what he brought them from {allˈɑːh}, Most High. He went out to them alone.

text: They did not do as he asked. They set their foolish ones and their slaves on him, insulting him and shouting at him, until people gathered round him and drove him to a walled garden belonging to ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa and Shayba ibn Rabiʿa, who were in it. The foolish ones of Thaqif who had followed him turned back, and he went to the shade of a grapevine and sat in it.

text: “O Allah, to You I complain of my weakness, my lack of means and how little people think of me. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You leave me? To a stranger who frowns at me, or to an enemy You have given power over my affairs? If You are not angry with me, I do not mind, but Your protection is wider for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face, by which the darknesses are lit and the affairs of this world and the next are set right, from Your anger coming down on me or Your displeasure falling on me. To You I turn until You are pleased. There is no power and no strength except through You.”

text: When the two sons of Rabiʿa, ʿUtba and Shayba, saw him and what he had met, they felt for him as kin. They called a Christian servant of theirs named ʿAddas and told him: “Take a bunch of these grapes, put it on this plate, then take it to that man and tell him to eat from it.” ʿAddas did so, and set it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “Eat.” When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his hand to it, he said “Bismillah”, then ate. ʿAddas looked at his face and said: “By Allah, the people of this land do not say these words.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “And which land are you from, ʿAddas, and what is your religion?” He said: “I am a Christian, a man from Nineveh.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “From the town of the righteous man Yunus ibn Matta.” ʿAddas said: “And how do you know who Yunus ibn Matta was?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He is my brother. He was a prophet, and I am a prophet.”

text: [Ibn ʿAbbas said:] The Prophet ﷺ was sent at the age of forty. He stayed thirteen years [in Makkah] receiving revelation, then he was commanded to emigrate, and he lived as an emigrant for ten years. He died at the age of sixty-three.
parts: [{ˈibn} Abbas said:] The Prophet , peace be upon him, was sent at the age of forty. He stayed thirteen years [in {mˈakka}] receiving revelation, then he was commanded to emigrate, and he lived as an emigrant for ten years. He died at the age of sixty-three.

text: His Hijrah, peace be upon him, was in the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal, in the thirteenth year after he was sent, and it was on a Monday.
parts: His Hijrah, peace be upon him, was in the month of Rabi al-Awwal, in the thirteenth year after he was sent, and it was on a Monday.

text: When Abu Bakr had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to emigrate, he had said to him: “Do not hurry. Perhaps Allah will give you a companion.” Abu Bakr hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meant himself, so he bought two riding camels and kept them at his house, feeding them to be ready for it.

text: Al-Waqidi said: he bought them for eight hundred dirhams.
parts: Al-Waqidi said: he bought them for eight hundred dirhams.

text: [ʿAʾisha said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never failed to come to Abu Bakr’s house at one end of the day or the other, morning or evening. Then, on the day Allah gave His Messenger ﷺ permission to emigrate and leave Makkah, he came to us in the midday heat, at an hour when he never came. When Abu Bakr saw him he said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not come at this hour unless something has happened.” When he came in, Abu Bakr moved aside on his couch for him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down. There was no one with him but me and my sister Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Send out whoever is with you.” He said: “O Messenger of Allah, they are only my two daughters. What is it, may my father and mother be your ransom?” He said: “Allah has given me permission to leave and emigrate.” Abu Bakr said: “The company, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “The company.” By Allah, I had never known before that day that anyone could weep from joy, until I saw Abu Bakr weeping that day.

text: Then he said: “O Prophet of Allah, these are two camels I had made ready for this.” They hired ʿAbdullah ibn Arqat (Ibn Hisham says he is also called ʿAbdullah ibn Urayqit), a man of Banu al-Duʾil ibn Bakr whose mother was from Banu Sahm ibn ʿAmr. He was an idol-worshipper, and he was to show them the road. They handed their two camels to him, and he kept them, grazing them, until the time they had agreed.
parts: Then he said: “O Prophet of {allˈɑːh}, these are two camels I had made ready for this.” They hired Abdullah {ˈibn} Arqat ({ˈibn} Hisham says he is also called Abdullah {ˈibn} Urayqit), a man of Banu al-Duil {ˈibn} Bakr whose mother was from Banu Sahm {ˈibn} Amr. text: As for ʿAli, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told him to stay behind and give back, on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the things people had left in his keeping. There was no one in Makkah who had something he feared for but left it with him, because they knew his truthfulness and his trustworthiness.
parts: As for Ali, the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, told him to stay behind and give back, on behalf of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, the things people had left in his keeping. There was no one in {mˈakka} who had something he feared for but left it with him, because they knew his truthfulness and his trustworthiness.

text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made up his mind [to leave], he came to Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, and the two of them went out through a small door at the back of Abu Bakr’s house.
parts: When the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, had made up his mind [to leave], he came to Abu Bakr {ˈibn} Abi Quhafa, and the two of them went out through a small door at the back of Abu Bakr’s house.

text: Then they made for a cave in Thawr, a mountain below Makkah, and went into it. Abu Bakr told his son ʿAbdullah to listen during the day to what people were saying about them, and to come to them in the evening with the day’s news. He told his freed slave ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra to graze his sheep during the day and bring them to them in the evening at the cave. So ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr spent his days among Quraysh, hearing what they were plotting and what they said about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr, then came to them in the evening and told them the news. ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra grazed with the shepherds of Makkah, and in the evening brought Abu Bakr’s sheep to them, and they milked and slaughtered. When ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr went back from them to Makkah in the morning, ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra followed his tracks with the sheep to cover them.

text: Ibn Jarir reported from some that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the cave of Thawr ahead of al-Siddiq, and told ʿAli to show him the way, and he caught up with him on the road. This is very strange, and against the well-known view that they left together.

text: Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with her, would bring them food in the evening, what they needed.
parts: Asma bint Abi Bakr, may {allˈɑːh} be pleased with her, would bring them food in the evening, what they needed.

text: [Abu Bakr] said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ while we were in the cave: “If one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet.” He said: “O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, when Allah is their third?”
parts: [Abu Bakr] said: I said to the Prophet , peace be upon him, while we were in the cave: “If one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet.” He said: “O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, when {allˈɑːh} is their third?”

text: Some writers of the Sira mention that when Abu Bakr said that, the Prophet ﷺ said: “If they come at us from here, we will go out from there”, and al-Siddiq looked and saw the cave open on the other side, with the sea joined to it and a ship tied up beside it.

text: This is not impossible for the Mighty Power, but it has not come with any chain, strong or weak, and we do not affirm anything on our own account.
parts: This is not impossible for the Mighty Power, but it has not come with any chain, strong or weak, and we do not affirm anything on our own account.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met al-Zubayr with a party of Muslims, merchants on their way back from al-Sham [to Makkah], and al-Zubayr gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr white clothes to wear.

text: The Muslims in Madinah heard that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left Makkah, and every morning they would go out to the lava field and wait for him until the midday heat drove them back. One day, after waiting a long time, they turned home. When they had gone into their houses, a Jewish man climbed one of their forts to look at something, and saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions dressed in white, shimmering in the mirage. He could not stop himself calling out at the top of his voice: “People of the Arabs, here is your good fortune that you have been waiting for!” The Muslims hurried to their weapons and met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the edge of the lava field. He turned with them to the right until he stopped with them among Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and that was on a Monday in the month of Rabiʿ al-Awwal.

text: Abu Bakr stood to greet the people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in silence. Those of the Ansar who came and had never seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began greeting Abu Bakr, until the sun reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr came and shaded him with his cloak. Then the people knew which one was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed among Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf for some ten-odd nights. He founded the mosque that was founded on taqwa, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in it.
parts: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, stayed among Banu Amr {ˈibn} Awf for some ten-odd nights. He founded the mosque that was founded on taqwa, and the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, prayed in it.

text: Then he rode his camel and went on, with the people walking beside him, until it knelt at the place of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah, where some of the Muslims were praying at that time. It was a place for drying dates belonging to Suhayl and Sahl, two orphan boys in the care of Asʿad ibn Zurara. When his camel knelt with him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “This, if Allah wills, is the place to stay.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the two boys and asked them the price of the drying place, to make it a mosque. They said: “No, we will give it to you, O Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused to take it from them as a gift until he had bought it from them. Then he built it as a mosque.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began carrying the mud bricks with them as they built it, saying as he carried them: “This load is not the load of Khaybar: this, our Lord, is more righteous and purer.” And he said: “O Allah, the reward is the reward of the Hereafter, so have mercy on the Ansar and the Muhajirun.”

text: [Ibn ʿUmar said] that in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was of palm branches, and its pillars were palm trunks.
parts: [{ˈibn} Umar said] that in the time of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was of palm branches, and its pillars were palm trunks.

text: [Anas said:] The Prophet ﷺ made a pact of brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar in our house.
parts: [Anas said:] The Prophet , peace be upon him, made a pact of brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar in our house.

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made brothers of his Companions from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and he said, as it reached us (and we seek refuge in Allah from saying of him what he did not say): “Become brothers for the sake of Allah, two by two.”
parts: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, made brothers of his Companions from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and he said, as it reached us (and we seek refuge in {allˈɑːh} from saying of him what he did not say): “Become brothers for the sake of {allˈɑːh}, two by two.”

text: Abu Bakr and Kharija ibn Zayd al-Khazraji were brothers; ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and ʿItban ibn Malik were brothers; Abu ʿUbayda and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh were brothers; and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and Saʿd ibn al-Rabiʿ were brothers.
parts: Abu Bakr and Kharija {ˈibn} Zayd al-Khazraji were brothers; Umar {ˈibn} al-Khattab and Itban {ˈibn} Malik were brothers; Abu Ubayda and Sad {ˈibn} Muadh were brothers; and Abd al-Rahman {ˈibn} Awf and Sad {ˈibn} al-Rabi were brothers.

text: [Anas said:] ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf came [to Madinah], and the Prophet ﷺ made him a brother of Saʿd ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Ansari. Saʿd offered to share his household and his wealth with him, half and half. ʿAbd al-Rahman said: “May Allah bless you in your household and your wealth. Show me the market.” And he made a profit of some dried curd and butter.
parts: [Anas said:] Abd al-Rahman {ˈibn} Awf came [to Madinah], and the Prophet , peace be upon him, made him a brother of Sad {ˈibn} al-Rabi al-Ansari. Sad offered to share his household and his wealth with him, half and half. Abd al-Rahman said: “May {allˈɑːh} bless you in your household and your wealth. Show me the market.” And he made a profit of some dried curd and butter.

text: [He ﷺ said:] “It is a true dream, if Allah wills. Stand with Bilal and teach it to him, and let him call it, for his voice is more beautiful than yours.” When Bilal called it, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab heard it in his house and came out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, dragging his cloak, saying: “O Prophet of Allah, by the One who sent you with the truth, I saw the same as he saw.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “To Allah be the praise [for that].”
parts: [He , peace be upon him, said:] “It is a true dream, if {allˈɑːh} wills. Stand with {bilˈɑːl} and teach it to him, and let him call it, for his voice is more beautiful than yours.” When {bilˈɑːl} called it, Umar {ˈibn} al-Khattab heard it in his house and came out to the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him,, dragging his cloak, saying: “O Prophet of {allˈɑːh}, by the One who sent you with the truth, I saw the same as he saw.” The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, said: “To {allˈɑːh} be the praise [for that].”

text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spent that night praying beside the stump of a tree there, often saying in his prostration “Ya Hayy, ya Qayyum”, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, repeating it and holding on to it, peace be upon him.
parts: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, spent that night praying beside the stump of a tree there, often saying in his prostration “Ya Hayy, ya Qayyum”, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, repeating it and holding on to it, peace be upon him.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out to reach the water before them, and when he came to the nearest water of Badr he stopped there.
parts: {ˈibn} {ishˈɑːk} said: The Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, set out to reach the water before them, and when he came to the nearest water of Badr he stopped there.

text: I was told by men of Banu Salima that al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jamuh said: “O Messenger of Allah, this place where we have stopped: is it a place Allah has brought you to, so that we may not move forward or back from it, or is it a matter of opinion, war and planning?” He said: “It is a matter of opinion, war and planning.” He said: “O Messenger of Allah, this is not the right place. Take the people on until we reach the water nearest to them, and stop there. Then we will stop up the wells beyond it, build a basin by it and fill it with water. Then we will fight them: we will drink and they will not.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You have given good advice.”

text: I say: the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that day were three hundred and thirteen men.
parts: I say: the Companions of the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, that day were three hundred and thirteen men.

text: [al-Baraʾ said:] We used to say that the people of Badr were three hundred and ten-odd, the same number as the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed it with him but a believer.
parts: [al-Bara said:] We used to say that the people of Badr were three hundred and ten-odd, the same number as the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed it with him but a believer.

text: Al-Bayhaqi said: The well-known view among the writers of the campaigns is that it was on the seventeenth night of the month of Ramadan.
parts: Al-Bayhaqi said: The well-known view among the writers of the campaigns is that it was on the seventeenth night of the month of {ɹamadˈɑːn}.

text: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari was asked about the day of Badr, and said: either the seventeenth, or the thirteenth …
parts: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari was asked about the day of Badr, and said: either the seventeenth, or the thirteenth …

text: [Ibn ʿAbbas said:] Some of the captives on the day of Badr had no ransom, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made their ransom that they should teach the children of the Ansar to write.
parts: [{ˈibn} Abbas said:] Some of the captives on the day of Badr had no ransom, so the Messenger of {allˈɑːh} , peace be upon him, made their ransom that they should teach the children of the Ansar to write.

text: The correct view is that of the majority: Uhud was in Shawwal of the year three, and the Trench in Shawwal of the year five after the Hijrah.
parts: The correct view is that of the majority: Uhud was in Shawwal of the year three, and the Trench in Shawwal of the year five after the Hijrah.

text: They agreed to lay down war between the people for ten years, in which people would be safe and hold back from one another; that whoever came to Muhammad from Quraysh without his guardian’s permission, he would send back to them, and whoever came to Quraysh from those with Muhammad, they would not send back to him; that between us there would be a sealed chest, with no stealing and no betrayal; and that whoever wished to enter into the pact and covenant of Muhammad could do so, and whoever wished to enter into the pact and covenant of Quraysh could do so. Khuzaʿa jumped up and said: “We are in the pact and covenant of Muhammad”, and Banu Bakr jumped up and said: “We are in the pact and covenant of Quraysh.” And that you go back this year and do not enter Makkah against us; and next year we will go out from it for you, and you will enter it with your companions and stay three days, with only a rider’s weapons, swords in their sheaths, and you will not enter it with anything else.
